questions.question: What are hardware devices that retrieve data from a computer system and further translate the received data into a form understandable to humans?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **__Output Devices__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• **Hardware devices** that **retrieve data** from a **computer system** and translate the received data into a form understandable to humans are known as **output devices.**
 
• These devices take **digital information from a computer **and convert it into a **human-readable format.**

Some common examples of output devices include:

 
• **Monitor/Display:** A visual output device that presents information in the** form of text, images, and graphics on a screen.**
 
• **Printer: **Prints digital data onto physical paper in the form **of text, images, or both.**
 
• **Speaker:** Converts digital audio data into an **audible sound, allowing users to hear sounds, music, or other audio output.**
 
• **Projector: **Displays computer-generated images or video onto a larger screen or projection surface, often used for presentations or home theater setups.
 
• **Headphones/Earphones: **Output devices that provide audio output directly to the user's ears, allowing for private listening.
 
• **Plotter:** A device used to produce high-quality, large-scale graphics or drawings based on computer instructions.

questions.question: Speed of ______ printer is measured in characters per second (CPS).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dot Matrix

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

Print resolution is measured as the number of Dots Per Inch (dpi).

 
• ​It can be said that Resolution (in terms of print) is a measure of the number of dots that a device can put in one square inch of page space.
 
• The higher the dot density, the higher the resolution of the print or scan.
 
• A printer with 600 DPI is a printer that prints 600 x 600 per square inch or 360,000 dots per inch.
 
• Increasing the DPI will make the size of the printed image smaller while decreasing the DPI will make the size of the printed image larger.

 

 
• Characters-per-second (cps) is a unit of measure used to describe the speed of dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers.
 
• Lines-Per-Minute (LPM) is the number of lines of text a printer is capable of producing in one minute. It is affected by factors such as text size, resolution, and colour.
 
• Pages per minute (PPM) is a printer speed measurement standard. It is the measurement standard for how fast a printer can print a standardized page.

questions.question: A message that tries to trick a person into providing information such as his social security number, bank account information or login username and password for a website is a type of cyber attack called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phishing.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phishing:**__

 __
 
• Phishing is the **attempt to acquire sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, and credit card details (and sometimes, indirectly, money), often for malicious reasons, by masquerading as a trustworthy entity in an electronic communication.**
 
• The first recorded use of the term** "phishing"** was in the cracking toolkit **AOHell created by Koceilah Rekouche in 1995.**
 
• **Types of phishing**:
 
 
• Email phishing
 
• Spear pishing
 
• Whaling and CEO Fraud
 
• Clone phishing
 
• Voice phishing SMS phishing
 
• Calendar phishing
 
• Page hijacking.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Macro Virus**__

 __
 
• **A macro virus **is a piece of malicious code written in the same macro language used in everyday applications, such as Microsoft Word, Excel, and Powerpoint.
 
• The attack code commonly hides in documents and spreadsheets and is activated as soon as you open the file.
 
• Once the macro virus has infected one of your applications, it triggers malware designed to cause damage to your computer and further spread the virus.
 
• Since the code runs on software and not on operating systems, it can infect any computer, even your Mac.
 
 
 
• **Zombie**__
 __
 
• **A Zombie** is a fictional character that can replicate itself.
 
 
 
• **Worm**__
 
 
• **A computer worm is a malicious program that replicates itself in order to spread to other computers.**

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) in a Central Processing Unit (CPU)?

options.text: It executes program instructions by performing calculations and logical comparisons.
It manages the data flow between the CPU and memory.
It controls the speed of the CPU fan.
It connects the CPU to peripheral devices.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) It executes program instructions by performing calculations and logical comparisons.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** is a critical component of the CPU that **executes program instructions** by performing calculations and logical comparisons.
 
• The ALU handles **arithmetic operations** like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• It also performs **logical operations** such as AND, OR, NOT, and XOR, which are essential for decision-making processes in programs.
 
• By executing these operations, the ALU enables the CPU to process data and run applications effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Control Unit (CU)** and the ALU together form the CPU's core, where the CU directs the operations and the ALU performs the actual data processing.
 
• The ALU can be found in various types of processors, including general-purpose CPUs, microcontrollers, and graphics processing units (GPUs).
 
• Modern CPUs may have multiple ALUs to handle parallel processing tasks, thereby improving performance and efficiency.
 
• The development and optimization of ALUs have been fundamental in advancing computer technology and enabling more complex computing tasks.

• **​A monitor** is an output device that displays visual information from a computer or other electronic device. Also referred to as a computer screen or display screen, a monitor is one of the most important components of a computer system.
 
• 
 
**A dot matrix printer** is a type of impact printer that uses a matrix of **small pins to strike an inked ribbon and create an image or text on paper**.

 
 
•

questions.question: Which of the following is a single user operating system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__MS-DOS.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An operating system that allows a single user to perform only one task at a time is called a Single-User Single-Tasking Operating System.
 
• Functions like printing a document, downloading images, etc., can be performed only one at a time. Examples include MS-DOS, Palm OS, etc.
 
• **Advantage:**
 
 
• This operating system occupies less space in memory.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantage:**
 
 
• It can perform only a single task at a time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are **four types of operating systems** -

 
 
• Real-time operating system.
 
• Single-User/Single-Tasking operating system.
 
• Single-User/Multitasking operating system.
 
• Multi-User/Multitasking operating system.
 
 
 
• A **real-time operating system** is designed to run real-time applications. It can be both single- and multi-tasking. Examples include Abbasi, AMX RTOS, etc.
 
• An operating system that allows a single user to perform more than one task at a time is called **Single-User Multitasking Operating System.**
 
• **Examples** include** Microsoft Windows and Macintosh OS.**
 
• It is an operating system that permits several users to utilize the programs that are concurrently running on a single network server. The single network server is termed as **"Terminal server". "Terminal client"** is software that supports user sessions. Examples include** UNIX, MVS,** etc.

questions.question: IBM 360 was developed in which of the following generations of computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Third Generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The IBM System/360 **was announced and developed in the** mid-1965s, during the period associated with third-generation computers.**
 
• Third-generation computers were defined by the use of **integrated circuits (ICs) or semiconductor chips, which represented a significant advancement over the previous generation's technology.**
 
• The** System/360** was a groundbreaking series of** compatible mainframe computers, allowing customers to upgrade from lower-cost models to larger systems without having to rewrite their applications.**
 
• It also introduced the** 8-bit byte to the commercial world, which remains a fundamental data management unit today.**
 
• **The S/360** was not just a computer but a whole series of computers that helped to establish the concept of a computer **"family".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation:**

 
 
• These computers** (late 1946s to mid-1959s) were based on vacuum tubes.**
 
• They were large, expensive, and generated a lot of heat.
 
• Examples include the **ENIAC and UNIVAC.**
 
 
 
• **Second Generation:**
 
 
• Second generation computers** (mid-1959s to mid-1965s) moved from vacuum tubes to transistors, which were smaller, faster, cheaper, and more reliable.**
 
• **IBM's 7000 series belongs to this generation.**
 
 
 
• **Fourth Generation:**
 
 
• These computers** (1971 to the mid-1980s) are characterized by microprocessors which contain many, sometimes millions, of ICs.**
 
• **Personal computers, such as the IBM PC, fall into this category.**

questions.question: ______ is the key circuit board holding the essential processing parts of a computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motherboard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motherboard**: The motherboard is the main circuit board of a computer.

 
 
• It houses the **CPU, RAM, and other essential components.**
 
• It also provides the electrical connections by which the other components of the system communicate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 

 **Firmware**
 
 
Firmware is a type of software that provides control, monitoring and data manipulation of engineered products and systems.

 
It's typically stored in the read-only memory of a hardware device.

 
 
 

 **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**
 
 
The CPU is the primary component of a computer that performs most of the processing inside the computer.

 
It's often called the "brain" of the computer.

 
 
 

 **Random Access Memory (RAM)**
 
 
RAM is a type of computer memory that can be read from and written to by the processor.

 
It's a volatile memory, meaning it loses its contents when the computer is turned off or restarted.

questions.question: What is used for holding program instructions that can't be changed throughout the life of the computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ROM**

 
 
• Read-Only Memory is a ROM in a computer.
 
• Read-only memory is a storage medium that permanently stores data on computers and electronic devices.
 
• The data stored in these chips is nonvolatile i.e. it is not lost when power is removed.
 
• There are five basic ROM types:
 
 
• ROM: Read-Only Memory.
 
• PROM: Programmable read-only memory.
 
• EPROM: Erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• EEPROM: Electrically erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• Flash memory: Flash memory, a type of EEPROM that uses in-circuit wiring. 
 
 
 
• BIOS uses Flash memory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Register**

 
 
• The smallest and fastest memory of a computer is registered memory located in the computer's central processing unit(CPU).
 
• It generally stores the most used instructions, data, etc. which are to be used by CPU.
 
• Control Unit is part of the CPU.
 
• It advises the input and output devices, and computer memory on how to respond to the instructions sent to the processor.
 
 
 
• **RAM**
 
 
• It stores data that the computer needs to use temporarily. So it is faster than the secondary storage devices. It is a volatile memory i.e. the data disappear from it when the power is off.
 
• It is known as the Read-Write Memory. i.e. the user can write information into RAM and read information from it.
 
• It is called random access since any memory location can be accessed randomly for reading and writing. The access time is the same for each memory location.
 
• It is usually called “temporary” memory, which means that when the system is shut down, the memory is lost.
 
 
 
• **Cache**
 
 
• A cache memory is used by the central processing unit of a computer to reduce the average cost time or energy to access data from the** main memory**. 
 
• Generally Cache memory is logically positioned between** CPU** and **main memory**.

questions.question: A User Interface is the part of _______ that allows the user to enter and receive information.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **operating system.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Computer software includes both system and application software, and it's the component that enables user interaction through a user interface**__.

 __
 
• The user interface (UI) is a software feature that allows users to interact with the computer, enter commands, and receive feedback.
 
• The UI can be graphical (GUI) or text-based (CLI), and is present in operating systems, apps, and other programs.
 
• Therefore, UI is not exclusive to the operating system but spans across all types of software.
 
• Examples of software with UI include:
 
 
• Operating systems like Windows, Linux, macOS.
 
• Applications like Microsoft Word, Google Chrome, VLC Media Player.
 
• Mobile apps and development tools.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operating System** is a type of system software that manages hardware and provides core UI elements like taskbars, file explorers, etc.
 
• **Computer Network** refers to interconnected systems that share resources but are not the source of UI themselves.
 
• **Hardware** refers to the physical components like keyboard, monitor, CPU – which are used by UI but do not provide it themselves.

questions.question: Which of the following options refers to the layout arrangement of different devices in a network?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Network topology.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Network topology** refers to the** physical and logical arrangement of nodes and connections** in a network.
 
• The **nodes** include devices such as **switches, routers, and software with switch and router features**.
 
• These topologies can come in a few different forms, including **star, bus, ring, mesh, and hybrid,** each of which has different strengths and weaknesses.
 
• **Physical topology **deals with the physical design of the network, including the** devices, location and cable installation,** while** logical topology** focuses on** how data is transferred within the network**.
 
• **Network topologies** are extensively used in the **architectural design of networks**, as it lays out the route that data takes between nodes and depicts how different nodes in a network are connected to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Open systems**

 
 
• An open system is a system that has external interactions. Such systems are capable of interconnecting with other systems, exchanging data, and functioning within a networked environment.
 
• In the context of computing, an open system refers to a computing device, software or system that uses an open-source model, allowing it to interact seamlessly with other systems.
 
 
 
• **Transmission mode**
 
 
• Transmission mode, also known as the communication mode, refers to the process of sending and propagating data between two devices within a network.
 
• They can be of different types such as simplex (one-way communication), half-duplex (two-way communication, but only one at a time), and full-duplex (two-way communication simultaneously).
 
 
 
• **Closed systems**
 
 
• A closed system is a type of system where interactions only happen among the system components and not the environment outside. They are self-contained and do not rely on exchanges with the external environment to function.
 
• In terms of computer systems, a closed system can also refer to a system with proprietary standards and protocols, which restricts its ability to interact seamlessly with other systems.

questions.question: 1 terabytes per second = ______ bytes per second
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**240**____.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A Terabyte (TB) is a measure of computer storage capacity that is approximately 2 to the 40th power, or 10 to the 12th power, which equals approximately a trillion bytes.
 
• A Terabyte is more precisely defined as 1,024 gigabytes (GB), while a petabyte consists of 1,024 TB.
 
• A tbyte, terabyte, or TB, is equal to 1,099,511,627,776 (240) bytes.
 
• However, the IEC defines a TB as equal to 1,000,000,000,000 (1012) bytes.

• 1 TB = 1024 gigabytes.
 
• The terabyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information.
 
• The prefix term was defined for the International System of Units in 1960.

questions.question: What is 'Phishing' in the context of network security?

options.text: A type of computer worm that spreads through email attachments.
An attack that floods a network with excessive traffic to disrupt its operation.
A social engineering attack that tricks users into revealing sensitive information.
A type of malware that spreads through infected USB drives.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A social engineering attack that tricks users into revealing sensitive information.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phishing** is a type of social engineering attack often used to steal user data, including login credentials and credit card numbers.
 
• It occurs when an attacker, masquerading as a trusted entity, dupes a victim into opening an email, instant message, or text message.
 
• The recipient is then tricked into clicking a malicious link, which can lead to the installation of malware, the freezing of the system as part of a ransomware attack, or the revealing of sensitive information.
 
• Phishing is one of the oldest and most widespread internet scams, and it continues to be a significant concern in network security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phishing attacks** can be conducted through various communication channels including email, social media, phone calls, and text messages.
 
• Common signs of phishing attempts include unsolicited requests for sensitive information, generic greetings, and suspicious links or attachments.
 
• To protect against phishing, users should verify the source of unexpected requests, use multi-factor authentication, and keep their software updated.
 
• Organizations often conduct **phishing awareness training** to educate employees about recognizing and responding to phishing attempts.
 
• Reporting phishing attempts to appropriate authorities can help in mitigating the risks and preventing future attacks.

questions.question: _____ means sending data or a file from your computer on the internet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uploading.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uploading** refers to the process of **sending data or a file from your computer **to a different location on the Internet.
 
• This could be to a **website, cloud storage service, email recipient, or another type of platform or server.**
 
• Common examples of uploading include **adding photos to a social media profile, submitting documents** through an online form, installing a website via FTP, or placing a video on a video-sharing site.
 
• The speed at which files upload depends on the** file size and the strength and speed **of your Internet connection.
 
• Once a file is uploaded, it can be **accessed, viewed, or downloaded** through the Internet, provided the necessary permissions are granted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deleting**

 
 
• Deleting refers to removing data or files from your system or a particular storage space on the Internet (like cloud storage or email).
 
• When a file is deleted, it is typically moved to a 'trash' or 'recycle bin' folder before it's permanently erased, allowing you a chance to restore the file if the deletion was a mistake.
 
 
 
• **Downloading**
 
 
• Downloading is the process of getting data or a file from the Internet or another system to your own computer.
 
• Examples include downloading a document from an email, saving an image from a website, or getting a software program from an official site.
 
• The downloaded files can be accessed or opened with an appropriate software application even when you're offline.
 
 
 
• **Accessing**
 
 
• Accessing in the context of computers and the Internet involves entering a system or retrieving information from it.
 
• This could refer to logging into an email account, opening a file on your computer, or visiting a website in a web browser.
 
• Accessing typically requires appropriate permissions, and may need a username, a password, or other types of authentication.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an open-source operating system?
questions.solution:
**__Windows__ **is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Among the options, only **Windows**__ is NOT an open-source operating system.
 
• __**Windows**__ is a closed source operating system marketed by Microsoft.
 
• Microsoft first introduced the Windows operating system on 20 November 1985.
 
• Closed Operating Systems are built with numerous codes and complex programming and that is called **source code. **
 
• An **Open-source Operating System** is the Operating System in which source code is visible publically and editable.
 
• The operating system is a collection of programs that controls the overall operations of the computer.
 
• An operating system is a **System software in computers.**
 
• It works as an interface between** the user and computer hardware components.**
 
• Examples of operating systems are:
 __
 
• Linux.
 
• Unix.
 
• DOS.
 
• Windows.
 
• Ubuntu.
 
• Embedded operating system.
 
• OpenBSD.
 
• Mac OS.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

Windows is an operating system, but it is NOT an open-source operating system.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device used to verify the legitimacy or originality of paper documents, especially cheques?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic ink character recognition.**__

__
 
• **MICR** is used by the banking industry to ease the processing and clearance of cheques and other documents.
 
• Numbers and characters found on the bottom of checks are printed using the Magnetic Ink.
 
• When a document that contains this ink needs to be read, it passes through a machine, which magnetizes the ink and then translates the magnetic information into characters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A card **reader is a data input device that reads and writes​ data from a card-shaped storage medium.

 
 
• A card reader is a hardware device.
 
 
 
• **Non-impact printers **print the characters without using ribbons.
 
 
• These printers print a complete page at a time so they are also called page printers.
 
 
 
• **Optical Mark Reader (OMR)** can be considered as a Scanning device. 
 
 
• Optical mark recognition is the process of capturing human-marked data from document forms such as surveys and tests.
 
• They are used to read questionnaires, multiple-choice examination papers in the form of shaded areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct categorisation of volatile semiconductor memory based on the data retention capability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SRAM and DRAM.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **SRAM (Static Random-Access Memory) and DRAM (Dynamic Random-Access Memory) **are both types of **volatile memory.**
 
• SRAM** retains its data as long as power is connected**. However, the data in DRAM **begins to decay in seconds and has to be periodically refreshed.**
 
• Volatile memory refers to computer memory that requires power to maintain the stored information. Once power is interrupted, the stored data is lost.
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory),** which can be further divided into SRAM and DRAM, is generally a type of volatile memory, but the term itself does not automatically signify volatility.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)**, on the other hand, is a type of **non-volatile memory.**
 
• It retains its data regardless of whether power is connected or not, and it cannot be easily rewritten or erased by normal computer operations.
 
• The primary advantage of SRAM and DRAM over other forms of memory is **their speed**.
 
• They are therefore commonly used for **primary storage and cache memory **in computing devices.

questions.question:
Which of the following parts of given URL is a 'domain name'?

http://www.india.in/tallybook/tallybook.xyz
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) www.india.in**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **www.india.in** is the domain name in the given URL.
 
• The domain name is a part of the URL that identifies a specific website or location on the internet.
 
• In this case, **www.india.in** is the unique address that directs to a specific website.
 
• The other parts of the URL, such as **http:**, **tallybook**, and **tallybook.xyz**, serve different purposes like protocol and paths within the website.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A domain name is crucial for navigating the internet, as it provides a human-readable address for accessing websites.
 
• Domain names are managed and regulated by organizations such as ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers).
 
• They are usually composed of a second-level domain (e.g., "india") and a top-level domain (e.g., ".in").
 
• Proper understanding of domain names is essential for web development, SEO, and digital marketing.

questions.question: Which of the following consists of an electronic writing area and a special ‘pen’ that works with it?
questions.solution:

questions.question: In the field of computing, what does ENIAC stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ENIAC stands for **Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer.**
 
• It is considered to be the first operational electronic digital computer in the United States, developed by **Army Ordnance to compute World War II ballistic firing tables. **
 
• The first all-electric computing machine was proposed by physicist John Mauchly in **1942** and was completed in** 1945**.
 
• The ENIAC weighed **30 tons, used 200 kilowatts of electric power and consisted of 18,000 vacuum tubes, 1,500 relays, and hundreds of thousands of resistors**, capacitors, and inductors.
 
• The ENIAC used** 20 single-number accumulators **as primary functional units.
 
• The ENIAC's field of the application included weather prediction, atomic-energy calculations, cosmic-ray studies, thermal ignition, random-number studies, wind-tunnel design, and other scientific uses.
